title: Our Heavenly Father, Hear
description: Our Heavenly Father, Hear in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 28, “"After This Manner Pray Ye."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our Heav-enly Fa-ther, hear The prayer we o-ffer now: Thy name be hal-lowed far and near, To Thee all na-tions bow.

lines: Thy name be hallowed far and near,
On earth be done in love,
While by Thy word we live;
And guide us to the end.
Of heaven and earth are Thine.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
